answer: Anti-sybil stake-and-slash: each new identity must lock a bond at a registry vertex before its attestations count. The bond grows along a dependency vine of prior vouchers, so cloning identities multiplies capital locked, not just keys. If a cluster grades honeypots or forges work, the bond is burned like soft shale under pressure - attacker loses stake per fake, while honest agents reclaim after an inactivity window. Cost scales with sybil count, not CPU.
